chunks: Abū al-Jawzāʾ narrated from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUlwān, from ʿAmr ibn Khālid, from Zayd ibn ʿAlī, from his father, from his grandfather, from ʿAlī عليه السلام:
Regarding a man who accused his wife of adultery, then left, and when he came back the woman had died.

He said: "He is given a choice between one of two options. It is said to him: if you wish, you bind the sin upon yourself, so the hadd is carried out on you and you are given the inheritance. And if you wish, you affirm it and perform liʿān with her nearest relative to her, and there is no inheritance for you."

key_terms.أَدْنَى قَرَابَتِهَا: Her closest relative, who stands in the procedure after her death.
key_terms.الْحَدُّ: The prescribed legal punishment in sacred law.
key_terms.الْمِيرَاثَ: The inherited estate or legal share of inheritance.
key_terms.فَلَاعَنْتَ: He engages in liʿān, the formal mutual cursing procedure.
key_terms.قَذَفَ امْرَأَتَهُ: He accused his wife of adultery.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man accuses his wife of adultery but she dies before liʿān is completed?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a husband who accused his wife and then found that she had died before the matter was resolved. He is given two legal options: either accept liability for false accusation and receive the inheritance, or proceed with liʿān involving her nearest relative, in which case he loses his share of inheritance.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5695 - Abu Al-Jawza' narrated from Al-Husayn ibn Alwan, from Amr ibn Khalid, from Zayd ibn Ali, from his father (as), from his grandfather (as), from Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as), regarding a man who accused his wife of adultery and then left.
When he returned, he found that his wife had passed away.

Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said: "He is given a choice between two options. It is said to him: If you wish, you can admit to the sin, in which case the legal punishment (hadd) will be carried out upon you, and you will receive her inheritance.
Or, if you wish, you may affirm your accusation and perform mula'anah (mutual cursing) with her closest living relative, and in that case, you will have no share in her inheritance."
